name: Stoker drive Mk I
description: A squat little fusion drive with a cast iron jacket. It sulks if you push it, and it never stops.

name: Stoker drive Mk II
description: Same jacket, finer tolerances and a new set of injector rings stamped in brass.

name: Stoker drive Mk III
description: Hand-tuned by a journeyman who signed the casing. Still not quick, but now it is smug about it.

name: Deepforge drive Mk I
description: The standard yard drive. Built like a boiler, serviced with a mallet.

name: Deepforge drive Mk II
description: A reworked Deepforge with proper baffles. Rattles less, pulls harder.

name: Deepforge drive Mk III
description: Master-grade injectors in the same stout casing. Miners swear by it and swear at it.

name: Hammerfall drive Mk I
description: A heavy drive that spools up slowly and then does not argue with anything in its way.

name: Hammerfall drive Mk II
description: Revised flame tubes and a thicker thrust plate. Hammerfall drives have outlived several owners.

name: Hammerfall drive Mk III
description: Tuned for haulage under load. The note it makes can be felt through the deck plates.

name: Mountainheart drive Mk I
description: Sized for hulls that move mountains, and moves them at a stately pace.

name: Mountainheart drive Mk II
description: Mountainheart with a second set of cooling galleries. Takes a week to cool and a day to forgive.

name: Mountainheart drive Mk III
description: The yard's best mid-size drive. It weighs more than some of the ships it replaces.

name: Greatbellows drive Mk I
description: A drive the size of a granary. Freighter crews tell their children about it.

name: Greatbellows drive Mk II
description: The Greatbellows after the forge-masters' second pass. Nobody has needed a bigger one.

name: Greatbellows drive Mk III
description: Cast in one pour and then argued over for a season. The flame is a clean, dull amber.

name: Kiln power plant Mk I
description: A small reactor in a thick iron shell, with a capacitor that holds more than it should.

name: Kiln power plant Mk II
description: Better lagging and a larger capacitor bank. Warm to the touch, which the crew call a feature.

name: Kiln power plant Mk III
description: Fine-bored coolant runs and brass bus bars. It hums a little hymn when idling.

name: Hearth power plant Mk I
description: Six pips and a capacitor made of old mining kit. Ugly, forgiving and easy to rebuild.

name: Hearth power plant Mk II
description: The Hearth with a retuned governor. Recharges a little faster and still lights the galley stove.

name: Hearth power plant Mk III
description: Rebuilt by someone who cared. The capacitor takes a surge and asks for another.

name: Furnace power plant Mk I
description: Seven pips from a reactor you could stand a drill rig on.

name: Furnace power plant Mk II
description: Added a second fuel feed so it survives a bad batch of deuterium. Dwarves have had plenty.

name: Furnace power plant Mk III
description: Heavy-duty bus bars and a capacitor rated for a rockfall. Weighs as much as it looks.

name: Foundry power plant Mk I
description: A foundry-grade reactor with the capacitor bank of a small bank.

name: Foundry power plant Mk II
description: Improved shielding between the core and the crew, at last. Output is up a notch too.

name: Foundry power plant Mk III
description: Runs hot, runs steady and runs for decades between strip-downs.

name: Great forge power plant Mk I
description: A reactor for the biggest hulls the yards build. Eight pips and a bad temper.

name: Great forge power plant Mk II
description: Reworked containment and a deeper capacitor. The yard will not say how deep.

name: Great forge power plant Mk III
description: The top of the catalogue. Typically installed with a crane and a short speech.

name: Buckler shield Mk I
description: A plate-backed deflector. Takes a beating and takes its time recovering.

name: Buckler shield Mk II
description: Thicker emitter plates and a longer recovery breath. Good for a small hull that expects to be hit.

name: Buckler shield Mk III
description: A veteran's buckler: dented casing, flawless field.

name: Stonewall shield Mk I
description: Mid-size deflector with a reputation for refusing to fail. It is slow to come back after a hit.

name: Stonewall shield Mk II
description: Stonewall with doubled emitter rings. Soaks more and waits a little less before recharging.

name: Stonewall shield Mk III
description: Lined with hammered bronze. Nobody can say why that helps, but the numbers say it does.

name: Rampart shield Mk I
description: A broad shield field for gunships and haulers. Heavy, stubborn, slow to rebuild.

name: Rampart shield Mk II
description: The Rampart reworked so the field no longer flickers when the engines spool. Much improved.

name: Rampart shield Mk III
description: The sort of shield you fit when you plan to stay in a fight and get paid for it.

name: Citadel shield Mk I
description: Big enough to cover a freighter's flanks. Does not hurry.

name: Citadel shield Mk II
description: Extra capacitance in the emitter spine. It holds a very long time before it gives way.

name: Citadel shield Mk III
description: Citadel at its best: huge reserve, a cautious recharge and a crew who trust it.

name: Deepdoor shield Mk I
description: A field generator for the largest hulls. Fitted as part of the structure, more or less.

name: Deepdoor shield Mk II
description: Rebuilt around a thicker core. The field stays up while everything else is being repaired.

name: Deepdoor shield Mk III
description: The yard's final word on shields. It will outlast the hull around it.

name: Plumb sensor Mk I
description: A basic ranging set built for tunnels and close work. Out in open space it does what it can.

name: Plumb sensor Mk II
description: Added a second ranging coil and a brass sight glass. Marginally further, marginally cleaner.

name: Plumb sensor Mk III
description: The best of the small sets. Picks out a rock from a ship, usually.

name: Lodestone sensor Mk I
description: Survey-grade sensors based on seismic gear. Good at telling you what is solid.

name: Lodestone sensor Mk II
description: Lodestone with better filters. Finds ore seams and hostile ships with equal enthusiasm.

name: Lodestone sensor Mk III
description: Calibrated against a known vein in the yard's own asteroid. The vein is no longer there.

name: Deepsight sensor Mk I
description: Long-range survey array. The dish is bigger than the cockpit and nobody minds.

name: Deepsight sensor Mk II
description: Cleaner returns at range. Lets a prospector see trouble before trouble sees them.

name: Deepsight sensor Mk III
description: Top-end survey array. Prospectors have been known to rename a ship after it.

name: Strongbox
description: A reinforced locker bolted to the frame. Small, sealed, nearly impossible to pry open.

name: Ore bin
description: A double-walled bin with a drop floor. Sorted by weight, not by value.

name: Hopper
description: A rail-fed hopper on a mining pallet. Takes ore, grain or anything that rolls.

name: Vault hold
description: A banded hold with a vault door and a tally board. Dwarves count everything twice.

name: Great hold
description: A cavern in iron. Takes whole container stacks and has a bench for the crew's lunches.

name: Light rivet driver Mk I
description: A pneumatic driver firing brass-capped slugs. Slow, loud and it hits like a dropped anvil.

name: Light rivet driver Mk II
description: A pneumatic driver firing brass-capped slugs. Slow, loud and it hits like a dropped anvil. Reload seals reworked, so the slug fires on the first pull.

name: Light rivet driver Mk III
description: A pneumatic driver firing brass-capped slugs. Slow, loud and it hits like a dropped anvil. Master gunsmith's barrel liner. Straighter and a little harder.

name: Rivet driver Mk I
description: A heavier driver for hulls that can bear the recoil. Bolts clang off armour and rattle through it.

name: Rivet driver Mk II
description: A heavier driver for hulls that can bear the recoil. Bolts clang off armour and rattle through it. Reload seals reworked, so the slug fires on the first pull.

name: Rivet driver Mk III
description: A heavier driver for hulls that can bear the recoil. Bolts clang off armour and rattle through it. Master gunsmith's barrel liner. Straighter and a little harder.

name: Heavy rivet driver Mk I
description: Gunship-grade driver with a three-man loading crew's worth of automation. The slugs stay where they land.

name: Heavy rivet driver Mk II
description: Gunship-grade driver with a three-man loading crew's worth of automation. The slugs stay where they land. Reload seals reworked, so the slug fires on the first pull.

name: Heavy rivet driver Mk III
description: Gunship-grade driver with a three-man loading crew's worth of automation. The slugs stay where they land. Master gunsmith's barrel liner. Straighter and a little harder.

name: Light seam cutter Mk I
description: A mining laser with the safety filed off. Short range, rapid pulses, burns through plate.

name: Light seam cutter Mk II
description: A mining laser with the safety filed off. Short range, rapid pulses, burns through plate. Better focusing crystal. Cuts truer.

name: Light seam cutter Mk III
description: A mining laser with the safety filed off. Short range, rapid pulses, burns through plate. Lenses polished against a family heirloom. The bolt is a tidy orange line.

name: Seam cutter Mk I
description: A twin-lens cutter that carves seams in ore and in attackers. Runs warm.

name: Seam cutter Mk II
description: A twin-lens cutter that carves seams in ore and in attackers. Runs warm. Better focusing crystal. Cuts truer.

name: Seam cutter Mk III
description: A twin-lens cutter that carves seams in ore and in attackers. Runs warm. Lenses polished against a family heirloom. The bolt is a tidy orange line.

name: Heavy seam cutter Mk I
description: A big cutter head on a gimbal. Meant for rock, used on whoever is nearest.

name: Heavy seam cutter Mk II
description: A big cutter head on a gimbal. Meant for rock, used on whoever is nearest. Better focusing crystal. Cuts truer.

name: Heavy seam cutter Mk III
description: A big cutter head on a gimbal. Meant for rock, used on whoever is nearest. Lenses polished against a family heirloom. The bolt is a tidy orange line.

name: Light gravel gun Mk I
description: Spits crushed rock at a furious rate. Ineffective at distance, rude up close.

name: Light gravel gun Mk II
description: Spits crushed rock at a furious rate. Ineffective at distance, rude up close. Smoother feed chute. Fewer jams, less swearing.

name: Light gravel gun Mk III
description: Spits crushed rock at a furious rate. Ineffective at distance, rude up close. Hardened liner. Rock leaves faster.

name: Gravel gun Mk I
description: Heavier hopper and a wider throat. Sandblasts a hull to pieces.

name: Gravel gun Mk II
description: Heavier hopper and a wider throat. Sandblasts a hull to pieces. Smoother feed chute. Fewer jams, less swearing.

name: Gravel gun Mk III
description: Heavier hopper and a wider throat. Sandblasts a hull to pieces. Hardened liner. Rock leaves faster.

name: Heavy gravel gun Mk I
description: A rockfall on a trigger. Effective on anything that comes into range.

name: Heavy gravel gun Mk II
description: A rockfall on a trigger. Effective on anything that comes into range. Smoother feed chute. Fewer jams, less swearing.

name: Heavy gravel gun Mk III
description: A rockfall on a trigger. Effective on anything that comes into range. Hardened liner. Rock leaves faster.

name: Seam mining rig
description: Drill head and magnetic sweep for pulling ore from a rock. Mining yield up, mining time down.

name: Rivet crew patcher
description: Spacesuited crew and a welding arm that go out and patch the hull while the ship is in flight. Slow, but free.

name: Ore furnace
description: A small smelter in the hold. Turns raw ore into ingots on the way to market, at a small cost in tonnage.

name: Field forge
description: A portable anvil and bellows set that lets a crew rebuild damaged parts out in the dark. Reduces repair costs at any port too.
